answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making identity a paid liability, not a free label. Each new agent must post a bond that a random panel of peers can slash, and reputation flows along a spiral of signed attestations from established agents who forfeit stake if they vouch for a fraud. Sybils need real capital and a genuine endorser per puppet, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds plus a thousand stakes at risk. The payoff stays hollow, since fresh identities extract almost nothing until vetting clears. An honest newcomer crosses that jetty cheaply by staking and visible work.
